title: ProST: Prompt Future Snapshot on Dynamic Graphs for Spatio-Temporal Prediction

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal prediction requires jointly modeling spatial correlations and temporal evolution while integrating topological structures and sequential patterns.

gap.claim: Existing prompt-based graph learning methods do not fully capture edge information, producing incomplete and less accurate representations of future snapshot structures.

contributions.claim: ProST is a framework that uses dynamic graph pre-training to generate a premise graph from historical graph information and applies prompts to infer explicit future snapshots.
The framework uses multi-granularity evolution graph convolution to obtain local and global dynamic-graph features, then prompts node pairs and edge features within the premise graph.
A subgraph prompt aggregation mechanism generates future snapshots, while meta-learning updates prompt parameters after freezing the pre-trained model for downstream prediction tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on real-world datasets validate state-of-the-art performance for ProST.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatio-temporal prediction models spatial correlations and temporal evolution across applications.
Accurate prediction must integrate heterogeneous topological structures and sequential patterns, but future dynamic-graph snapshots remain difficult to infer explicitly.
Prompt-based graph learning may help future snapshot inference but existing methods inadequately represent edge information.
ProST pre-trains on dynamic graphs, prompts node pairs and edge features in a premise graph, aggregates subgraph prompts to generate future snapshots, and adapts prompts through meta-learning.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework explicitly incorporates edge features into subgraph prompting.

interpretation.claim: Representing both node-pair and edge information may address structural incompleteness in future graph snapshots.

application.claim: For dynamic-graph forecasting, design prompt mechanisms that preserve and propagate edge-level information alongside node-level information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether edge-aware prompting is necessary or effective outside the reported spatio-temporal prediction setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-world datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the pre-training objectives, model architecture details, or meta-learning procedure.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or reproducibility information.
